correctness.rationale: An explicit LCF-defined graph gives a complete finite shortest-path matrix and six distance-four triples. At r=2 the two bipartition flag complexes are 3-fold joins of 3-point discrete spaces, each a wedge of eight two-spheres. The cover U,V collapses to these sides, its intersection is precisely the connected 18-vertex, 27-edge incidence graph, and null maps into simply connected U,V imply a homotopy-pushout wedge of 8+8+10=26 two-spheres. A separate complete acyclic 99-pair Hasse matching of all 225 faces leaves one critical vertex and 26 critical two-cells, independently proving the integral wedge. 4095 scale-three simplices exactly form a six-triad join; r=1 and r=4 are respectively the original graph and a full simplex. All persistence intervals then follow from disjoint homology degrees. The embedded verifier runs without nonstandard packages; mod-two boundary ranks corroborate but are not substituted for integral homotopy.

value.rationale: A natural 18-vertex highly symmetric incidence graph receives a complete integral classification at the missing first post-girth-stability scale, rather than a trivial negative check. The structural split 8+8+10 captures two side-geometry sphere wedges and a suspended incidence graph, and explains a significant transition in its graph-metric homology from 10 circles to 26 two-spheres. Together with the credited scale-three join, it fixes the previously missing degree-two barcode and completes a canonical graph-metric persistence example; precise natural invariant, meaningful mathematical motivation, and reproducible proof make the value independent of a family-level theorem.
